extracted.intended_audience: high-school students preparing for/participating in Chinese regional mathematical olympiads and coaches
extracted.subtask_description: Working on and writing solutions to high-school level mathematical-olympiad problems (geometry, number theory, combinatorics, inequalities) of the type used in China Girls' and China Western Mathematical Olympiads; includes contest-format procedural rules shown on the page.

rubrics_metrics.name: Participant eligibility (China Western Mathematical Olympiad)
rubrics_metrics.description: Students of grade 10 and 11, from Kazakhstan, Hong Kong, Macau and West China, are invited to take part in the China Western Mathematical Olympiad.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This states the target participant group / regional eligibility for the contest; used to determine who may enter the competition in the listed years.

rubrics_metrics.name: Competition duration and scheduling
rubrics_metrics.description: The competition lasts for 2 days; there are 4 problems to be completed within 4 hours each day (example schedules shown: First Day 8:00–12:00, Second Day 8:00–12:00).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifies contest timing and per-day problem load — relevant for planning time management and estimating per-problem time. The page lists concrete example dates/times for specific years (e.g., China Girls' MO Aug 12–13 2005 with 8:00–12:00 sessions).

rubrics_metrics.name: Problem presentation and solution expectations
rubrics_metrics.description: Problems are stated precisely (e.g., 'Find all positive integers n such that ...', geometric configuration with labeled points) and typically expect rigorous proofs or constructions; each problem is credited to a proposer and solutions include a formal proof followed by remarks (alternative approaches, generalizations, or comments).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Indicative of the expected solution style/quality: full proofs with clear logical steps, often accompanied by a 'Remark' discussing alternative methods or observations. Problems cover diverse topics (number theory, combinatorics, geometry, inequalities) and often require proof-based reasoning rather than computations only.
